At around age 50 I suffered my first-ever anxiety attack. OMG did that suck. If you've ever had one, you'll know.

I kept getting them, and frankly, they were unbearable.

So I found a good shrink, and I talked candidly about every uncomfortable thing I could, and then I did what she told me to do. I started to feel noticeably better after a couple of weeks, and I was pretty much over it after about nine months.

The reason I'm mentioning this is because it's a pretty safe bet that if you're feeling controlled by your fears, even occasionally, than you are probably having some trouble with anxiety too. Many people who have it, don't realize that they have it.

There's two tricks to it, I think. The first is to find a good shrink who you respect, because if you don't respect them you won't do the difficult things they suggest. Trust your gut and walk away if the one you picked at first isn't right for you.

Second, don't try to be likable. Show your weakness, and show the things you are most ashamed of, without a filter. If you start to feel the need to protect your self-esteem, remember that your self-esteem isn't doing you any favors right now. If ever there is a place for raw candor, it is here.

"I will not fear. Fear is the mind-killer. Fear is the little death that brings total obliteration. I will face my fear. I will permit it to pass over me and through me, and when it is gone there will be nothing. Only I will remain."
